title: How to Escape Group Chat Hell
gist: Group chats have become the default coordination layer for American social life, with a YouGov poll showing over a third of under-30 adults juggling four or more threads; the author offers a personal boundary-setting framework (triage, leave, mute, go direct) for coping with the overload.

insights.claim: A YouGov poll found that 34 percent of US adults under 30 are in at least four group chats via text or messaging apps, and 3 percent are in more than 20 distinct group chats.
insights.speaker: Reece Rogers
insights.so_what: Quantifies how deeply group messaging has penetrated daily life for younger users, a relevant usage baseline for any product or feature built around group chat, notifications, or attention.
insights.quote: 34 percent of adults under 30 said they are in at least four group chats, whether via text or other messaging app.
insights.locator: paragraph beginning 'Group chats are dominating the social lives'

insights.claim: Group chats have expanded beyond young people into a default coordination tool for nearly every social occasion, spanning WhatsApp, Instagram group threads, and iMessage across generations (e.g. book clubs, group trips, family reunions).
insights.speaker: Reece Rogers
insights.so_what: Signals group messaging is now cross-platform social infrastructure rather than a youth-specific behavior, widening the addressable use case for chat-app features like custom stickers, backgrounds, and notification controls.
insights.quote: All attempts at social interactions now spark a new group message.
insights.locator: paragraph beginning 'These group chats are not just for the young folk'

insights.claim: The author's coping framework for group-chat overload is to triage threads into a short list of essential ones, leave the rest (especially event-based chats once their purpose is served), mute or use Do Not Disturb settings for kept threads, and personalize the chats worth staying in.
insights.speaker: Reece Rogers
insights.so_what: A repeatable personal-productivity heuristic for managing notification overload that maps onto how messaging apps could better design granular per-thread notification and archival controls.
insights.quote: Make a short list of what you actually want to participate in and stay there.

insights.claim: The author argues that shifting from group-chat banter to direct one-on-one texting is the better way to cultivate relationships, even though group chats provide a bigger 'dopamine rush' from memes and reaction emojis.
insights.speaker: Reece Rogers
insights.so_what: Reflects a broader tension between engagement-optimized group features (reactions, stickers) and users' own sense that they weaken relationship quality versus direct messaging.
insights.quote: cultivating relationships often happens best with one-on-one moments.
